newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian stocks retreat as demand for shares wanes.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian stocks retreat as demand for shares wanes.

text.p: Several Nigerian blue chips lost ground on Wednesday as demand for shares fell, dealers said.
The all-share index slipped to 8,713.99 from 8,716.59 on Tuesday.
"There just don't seem to be many investors around. Only about 1.2 million shares changed hands," said one broker.
Among the key stocks that lost out were Unipetrol, which fell by 50 kobo to 70.50 naira.
United Bank for Africa fell by 35 kobo to 12.40 naira while Union Bank was down 20 kobo to 51.20 naira. The two are among Nigeria's top three banks.
Oil stock Agip and First Bank each lost 10 kobo to 23.90 naira and 15.30 naira, respectively.
Top on the gainers list was food and beverages pace-setter Nestle Foods Plc, which shot up by 80 kobo to 82.00 naira, consolidating its position as the highest priced stock.
"Nestle is still profiting from the impressive results it declared last week," said one trader.
Other gainers were Mobil and BOC Gases, formerly Industrial Gases Plc which rose 30 kobo apiece to 63.50 naira and 13.50 naira respectively.
Their appreciation was on expectation that they would announce good trading results soon, dealers said.
Guinness, which rose by 15 kobo on Tuesday when it posted an improved full year profit for last year, rose a modest 10 kobo on Wednesday to 8.75 naira.
